courses.title: Civil Engineering and Design Drafting
courses.description: An overview of the different technical areas of civil engineering and career opportunities by covering foundational knowledge of engineered public infrastructure along with their appropriate design guidelines and standards. In the context of civil engineering problems, exposure to foundational professional skills including problem solving, technical communications and visualizing problems and solutions in 3D, introducing the student to engineering design.Composition of design and construction drawings using CAD software and hand drafting. Corequisite(s): CE 1001L or CE 127L; and College Level Math.
courses.prerequisites: BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM or MSCE major.

courses.title: Civil Engineering and Design Drafting Laboratory
courses.description: Graphical representations for Civil Engineers. Introduction to engineering design in the different areas of Civil Engineering. Basics of civil engineering, multidisciplinary conceptual design processes and visualization of public and private infrastructure.Composition of design and construction drawings using CAD software and hand drafting. Corequisite(s): CE 1001 or CE 127; and College Level Math.
courses.prerequisites: BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Surveying Engineering
courses.description: Surveying methods, horizontal and vertical controls, traversing and adjustment, error analyses. Route location and layout. Horizontal and vertical alignments, profiles and sections. Fundamentals of construction layouts and staking. Area and volume computations, earthwork. State plane coordinates system. Requirements of tract maps. Corequisite(s): CE 1011L , CE 134L, or ETC 131L; MAT 1140 or MAT 114, MAT 1300 or MAT 130.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 1001 , CE 1101 , CE 127 or ETC 130; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Surveying Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Use and care of surveying instruments, field procedures and note-keeping for basic surveying measurements and computations for engineering project control, topographic mapping, and construction layout. Field assignments include determination of pace factor, chaining/taping, differential, and three-wire leveling, measurement of a closed traverse, compass rule adjustment, staking a building envelope, and topographic survey and mapping. Corequisite(s): CE 1011 , CE 134, or ETC 131; and MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 130, or MAT 1300 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 1001L , CE 1101L , CE 127L, or ETC 130L; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the most common construction materials: aggregate, concrete, masonry, asphalt, steel, and wood. The mechanical behavior of construction materials under static, dynamic, and environmental loads. The production, internal structure, use and testing of construction materials will also be discussed. Introduction to standards and specifications for construction materials. Corequisite(s): CE 221L or CE 2030L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, or CE 2051 ; CHM 121 or CHM 1210 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Preparation of concrete and asphalt test specimens in the lab and then measure the strength and deformation properties of these and other construction materials using specialized laboratory equipment.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, or CE 2051 ; CHM 121L or CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Engineering Statics
courses.description: Cross Listed as: ARO 2041 Two and three-dimensional equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies. Principles of friction. Properties of areas including centroids, centers of gravity, and moments of inertia. Distributed loads. Analysis of 2D and 3D trusses, frames and machines. Static equilibrium and statically indeterminate systems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 115, or MAT 130; C or better in PHY 1510 or PHY 131; and C of better in PHY 1510L or PHY 131L.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Plane stress and strain. Principal stresses and strains, Mohr’s Circle. Properties of materials, stress strain diagrams. Generalized Hooke’s Law for isotopic materials. Design loads, working stresses, and factor of safety. Statically indeterminate axially-loaded members. Torsional shearing stresses and displacements. Combined axial and torsional loads. Flexural and transverse shear stresses. Shear and moment diagrams. Beams of two materials. Buckling loads for isolated bars.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 214, ETT 210, CE 2041 , ARO 2041 , or ETM 2101 .

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: An introduction to fluid properties and mechanics of incompressible fluids and the machines that add energy to, or remove energy from a pressurized system. During the course we develop the topics of conservation of Mass, Energy and Momentum in pressurized systems along with an examination of centrifugal pumps, their mechanics, and their performance characteristics.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 214, ETT 210, CE 2041 , ARO 2041 , or ETM 2101 .

courses.title: Computer Programming and Numerical Methods
courses.description: Numerical methods for civil engineering are algorithms developed by mathematicians and computer scientists to solve various problems in civil engineering. These algorithms should be implemented in computers. Detailed discussion on the concepts of algorithms widely used in civil engineering. Use of object-oriented programming language (such as Visual Basic and Python), Excel and MATLAB to implement algorithms to solve civil engineering problems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 224, MAT 2240 , or MAT 216.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You Laboratory
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Engineering Geology I
courses.description: [GE 5D] Fundamentals of geology applied to engineering problems. Includes rock and soil properties, structure, erosion, sedimentation, groundwater flow, seismic explorations, rock/soil movements, and project site evaluations. Individual and group study of selected engineering geology problems or case studies. Corequisite(s): GSC 3210L .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Engineering Geology I Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5D] Laboratory investigation of geology aspects of engineering problems. Includes rock and soil properties, structure, erosion, sedimentation, groundwater flow, seismic explorations, rock/soil movements, landslide hazard assessment, ground motion analysis, liquefaction susceptibility and general site evaluations. Individual and group study of selected engineering geology problems. Instruction is carried out in the field and laboratory. Corequisite(s): GSC 3210 .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: App. of Stats in Engineering
courses.description: Statistical conclusion for problems observed in industry and business. Descriptive statistics, discrete and continuous distributions, hypothesis testing, control charts, factorial experiments and regression analysis.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 214, MAT 215, MAT 216, MAT 224, or MAT 1150 .

courses.title: Ethical Concepts in Technology and Applied Science
courses.description: [GE 3C or 5D] Explores ethics of engineers, scientists, and others involved with technology related to values, philosophy, ethical theory and practice, moral reasoning, morality in law and codes, professional standards, and societies-case studies. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: [GE 2] Integration techniques including integration by parts, integrals of trigonometric products, partial fractions, substitution and trigonometric substitution. Hyperbolic functions. Improper Integrals, sequences and series, polar coordinates, parametric equations and conic sections.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB >=3, AP Calc BC >=3, or C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Introduction to vectors, dot product, cross product, equations of lines and planes, calculus of vector valued functions, introduction to multivariable functions, differential calculus of multivariable functions, the chain rule, applications including extreme problems and Lagrange multipliers, integral calculus of multivariable functions, double and triple integrals, applications of double and triple integrals, line and surface integrals of vector fields, Green’s Theorem, the Divergence Theorem, Stokes’ Theorem.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Elementary Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
courses.description: Separable and linear ordinary differential equations; numerical and analytical solutions. Linear algebra: vectors in n-space, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization; applications to the study of systems of linear differential equations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Introduction to Newtonian Mechanics
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to mechanics, including Newton’s laws, vectors, statics, kinematics, conservation laws, rotational motion, Newtonian gravity, fluids, and simple harmonic motion. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ( MAT 1150 can be concurrent).

courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments in Newtonian mechanics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introduction to Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, including electrostatics, dc circuits, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, and Maxwell’s equations. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 115 or MAT 1150 ; and C- or better in PHY 132, PHY 132B, PHY 1510B or PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introductory Laboratory on Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Infrastructure Economics and Public Policy
courses.description: The role of infrastructure in society, including social, political, and economic impacts. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation of costs and benefits of infrastructure projects, including assessments of intangible benefits such as environmental protection. Assessing the merits of competing projects within the context of scarce resources. Financing private sector and public sector projects. Public policy related to infrastructure.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 114 or MAT 1140 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Properties and behavior of engineering materials including stress-strain relations, strength, deformation mechanisms, strength, deformation, and fracture. Experimental techniques common to structural engineering, interpretation of experimental data, comparison of measurements to numerical/analytical predictions, and formal, engineering report writing. Corequisite(s): CE 2051 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 2041 .

courses.title: Environmental Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to multifaceted areas of environmental engineering, by becoming familiar with different aspects of environmental engineering related to the application of scientific and engineering principles to control the environment. Environmental chemistry, mass balance, reaction kinetics, biological growth models, risk assessment, water pollution, solid waste, hazardous waste, energy, noise pollution, air pollution, soil pollution, and remediation. Corequisite(s): CE 3201L .
courses.prerequisites: CHM 121 or CHM 1210 ; CHM 121L or CHM 1210L ; CE 2061 or ME 311; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Emphasize multifaceted areas of environmental engineering, by providing learning hands-on experience in different aspects of environmental engineering related to water treatment, water reclamation, sustainability, air pollution, waste management, and site remediation. Corequisite(s): CE 3201 .
courses.prerequisites: BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Water Resources Engineering
courses.description: Water Resources Engineering is a study of water within the surface and subsurface. Analysis and design of surface hydrology, groundwater (subsurface) hydrology and open channel flow hydraulics. A deeper knowledge and appreciation of the following topics will be covered: statistics, watersheds, precipitation, evaporation, infiltration, discharge calculations, subsurface flow calculations, critical flow, uniform flow, non-uniform flow, culverts and open drainage design.
courses.prerequisites: CE 2061 , ME 311, or ETT 310; CE 2070 , CE 303, or CE 303A ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to geotechnical engineering covering the behavior of soil and rock as engineering materials. Topics include: soil classification, water flow in soils, stress-strain properties, and applications in slope stability and foundation design. Corequisite(s): CE 2061 , ME311, or ETT 310; and CE 3401L or CE 327L.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 115, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 2240 , MAT 131, MAT 2140 , or MAT 1310 ; C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, ETM 2201 , or CE 2051 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Application of geotechnical engineering principles to a design project; use of standard soil mechanics laboratory tests. Oral presentation of completed project. Corequisite(s): ETT 310, ME 311, or CE 2061 ; and CE 3401 or CE 326.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 115, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 2240 , MAT 131, MAT 2140 , or MAT 1310 ; C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, ETM 2201 , or CE 2051 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
courses.description: Overview of water policies, engineering approaches to protect water quality, drinking water standards, and unit processes used in a conventional water and wastewater treatment systems. Theory and conceptual design of systems to produce drinking water and treat municipal wastewater are discussed, as well as reactor theory, process kinetics, and models. Corequisite(s): CE 4201L .
courses.prerequisites: CE 332 or CE 3211 ; CHM 121L or CHM 1210L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Water and Wastewater Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience in analyzing water and wastewater samples using physical, chemical, and biological tests to assess quality and meet professional standards. Emphasis on practical lab skills, safety protocols, quality assurance, calculations, and result interpretation for both drinking water and wastewater treatment. Generative AI is integrated to streamline data analysis, and for the creation of reports for public communications relevant to engineering practice. Corequisite(s): CE 4201 .
courses.prerequisites: CE 332 or CE 3211 ; CHM 121L or CHM 1210L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Applied Hydrology
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5211 Hydrology as it is applied to storm water management. Evaluation of the ever changing regulations associated with storm water quality. Use/develop stochastic and process based hydrologic and hydraulic models. Based on the water quality regulations, hydrologic analysis and hydraulic analysis develop engineering solutions to the urban watershed. Further details will be provided associated with hydrographs, river routing and reservoir routing.
courses.prerequisites: CE 332 or CE 3211 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Environmental Remediation
courses.description: Fundamentals of physical, chemical, and biological environmental remediation and cleanup. Environmental chemistry, environmental microbiology, water contaminations, soil contaminations, air contaminations, physical methods, chemical methods, biological methods, pollution prevention strategies, regulations and future trends.
courses.prerequisites: CE 351 or CE 3201 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Hydraulics and Water Resources Laboratory
courses.description: Practical and hands-on course, with the opportunity to apply the principles of fluid mechanics, hydraulics and hydrology to real-world scenarios. Designed to complement the theoretical knowledge gained in fluid mechanics and water resources engineering courses. Provides students with essential laboratory skills.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 3211 .

courses.title: Role of Design Professionals In Society
courses.description: [GE 4C] The unique role of design professionals in society, and the associated privileges and responsibilities. Social, economic, historical, legal, and political aspects of professional practice, as well as ethics, social responsibility, regulatory requirements, professional liability, and the consequences of failures.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Construction Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: A study of the format, guidelines and practices of construction drawings and specifications for buildings and heavy construction. Architectural, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and landscape drawings. Properties of materials used in building and heavy construction. Methods of fabrication and installation of construction materials. Fundamental concepts of project management and practices. Corequisite(s): CE 3101L .
courses.prerequisites: CE 1101 , CE 1001 , CE 128L, or ETC 140L; CE 1101L , CE 1001L , CE 128L, or ETC 140L; MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 130, or MAT 1300 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Construction Engineering Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: A study of the format, guidelines and practices of construction drawings and specifications for buildings and heavy construction. Architectural, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and landscape drawings. Properties of materials used in building and heavy construction. Methods of fabrication and installation of construction materials. Fundamental concepts of project management and practices. Corequisite(s): CE 3101 .
courses.prerequisites: CE 1101 , CE 1001 , CE 128L, or ETC 140L; CE 1101L , CE 1001L , CE 128L, or ETC 140L; MAT 1140 , MAT 114, MAT 130, or MAT 1300 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Engineering Geomatics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Fundamentals of geomatics to support civil engineering. Introduction to Photogrammetry and remote sensing principles, GPS constellation, GIS and LiDAR applications. Foundation of Public Land Survey System, boundary surveys and descriptions. Subdivisions and map production in civil engineering projects.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; CE 134 or CE 1011 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Structural Analysis I
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Classification of structures, types of framing systems and loading, the statics and stability of determinate structures, and the methods of calculating deformations of determinate beams, frames, and trusses. An introduction to statically indeterminate structures is included based on the Method of Consistent Deformations. As such, it establishes a foundation for further study in Structural Analysis II and structural design in reinforced concrete, masonry, steel, timber, etc. Corequisite(s): CE 305L or CE 3501L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, ETM 2201 , or CE 2051 ; C- or better in MAT 115, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 2240 , MAT 131, or MAT 1310 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Structural Design Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Evaluation of loading demand on buildings constructed using three primary structural materials: steel, concrete and wood. The essential concepts of structural design are introduced and applied to evaluating demand on a prototypical five-story building constructed using these different materials. The construction assemblies are developed and evaluated and hierarchy and load path of vertical and lateral load resisting systems is investigated. Finally, using acquired knowledge, a case study of the selected existing buildings is performed. Corequisite(s): CE 304 or CE 3501 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 218, ETT 220, ETM 2201 , or CE 2051 ; C- or better in MAT 115, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 2240 , MAT 131, or MAT 1310 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Transportation Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Understanding of the history and operation of several principal modes of transportation including highways, air, inland waterways, railroads, coast shipping and ocean transportation. Application of various design principles to carry out basic aspects of transportation engineering design. Introduction to the fundamental concepts behind the design of transportation modes such as operational and vehicular characteristics, traffic control, transportation planning and human factors. Corequisite(s): CE 3601L .
courses.prerequisites: CE 134 or CE 1011 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Transportation Engineering Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Understanding of transportation engineering in terms of planning and design. The focuses are on the interchange geometric design, traffic impact study consisting of highway capacity calculation and traffic volume forecast and distribution, design of traffic signal including phasing and timing optimization and pole and conductor schedule, and parking facility design per ADA guidelines. The software packages used include Inroads, Synchro Studio and Microstation. Corequisite(s): CE 3601 .
courses.prerequisites: CE 134 or CE 1011 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Solid and Hazardous Waste Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Principles of integrated solid waste management and fundamentals of hazardous waste management and engineering. Waste generation, storage, collection, transfer, transport, processing, recovery, disposal of municipal and industrial solid waste. Hazardous and industrial waste identification, accumulation, minimization, transport, and development of a hazardous waste contingency plan to comply with disposal restrictions.
courses.prerequisites: CE 351L or CE 3201L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Water Reclamation and Desalination
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Introduction to water reclamation and reuse. The following topics will be discussed: water quality characteristics of importance, regulations, risk assessment, irrigation with reclaimed water, industrial uses of reclaimed water, urban non-irrigation uses of reclaimed water, direct and indirect potable reuse with reclaimed water, and contaminants of emerging concerns.
courses.prerequisites: CE 3201 ; CHM 121L or CHM 1210L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Air Quality Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Basic concepts in physics and chemistry of the atmosphere. Production, transformation, transport, and removal of air pollutants. The problems of photochemical smog, the greenhouse effect and climate change, stratospheric ozone, acid rain, and visibility. Analytical techniques for gases and particles. Numerical simulation of air pollution. Health and environmental effects of air pollution.
courses.prerequisites: CE 351 or CE 3201 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Unit Operations and Processes in Environmental Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5271 The study of various physical, chemical and biological operations and processes used in the professional practice of environmental engineering (water treatment, wastewater treatment, and soil remediation). Topics covered will be selected from areas such as reactor hydrodynamics, oxidation-reduction, coagulation-flocculation, chemical precipitation, ion exchange, adsorption process, biological oxidation, anaerobic digestion, activated sludge. Corequisite(s): CE 4271L .
courses.prerequisites: CE 3201 ; CE 3211 ; and BSCE, BSCET, or BSCEM.

courses.title: Unit Operations and Processes in Environmental Engineering Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5271L Covers the use of various physical, chemical and biological unit operation processes used for treatment of water, wastewater, stormwater and soil remediation as done in the professional practice of environmental engineering. Topics covered will be selected from areas such as reactor hydrodynamics, oxidation-reduction, coagulation-flocculation, chemical precipitation, ion exchange, adsorption process, biological oxidation, anaerobic digestion, activated sludge. Corequisite(s): CE 4271 . Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 , CE 3201 , and undergraduate standing.

courses.title: River Mechanics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5280 Foundation for understanding geomorphology, sediment transport and erosion in the river environment. Sediment properties; resistance to flow; incipient motion and bedforms; geomorphology; sediment transport; river stability; and river restoration. Conceptual design techniques will be introduces about natural and urban runoff.
courses.prerequisites: CE 332 or CE 3211 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Sustainable Operations and Practices for Green Stormwater Infrastructure
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Stormwater management (operations and practices) that protect, restore, or mimic the natural water cycle are referred to as Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI). GSI are engineered systems that utilize “natural” or “green” approaches to manage stormwater. Provides an introduction to fundamentals of GSI in the three categories: Natural Treatment Systems (lakes, wetlands, etc.), Mechanical Process Systems (screen, pumps, hydrodynamic separators, etc.), Passive Systems (Infiltration wells, bioswale, etc.). Reviews all accepts of funding, design, construction, optimization, water quality, operations & maintenance.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CE 3211 and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Subdivision Engineering and Land Survey Descriptions
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: History of land ownership and transfer of title; types of documents of land conveyance; forms of legal descriptions of public and private lands; interpretation of maps and documents for the physical survey location of land boundaries. Principles of precise description and writing of land boundaries; study of easements; value of monuments. Engineering and surveying methods in land use planning, design, and construction of subdivision development projects. Corequisite(s): CE 4321L , and CE 3211 or CE 332.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Subdivision Engineering and Land Survey Descriptions Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Precise description and writing of land boundaries and easements. Applications in land use planning, design, and construction of subdivision development projects. Corequisite(s): CE 4321 , and CE 3211 or CE 332.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: GIS Applications in Engineering and Remote Sensing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: GIS in engineering practice. Applications in environmental, water resources and transportation engineering. Spatial data structures (vector, raster). Data input and conversion. Terrain modeling and representation. Database management systems. Spatial and network analysis. Web mapping. Fundamentals of remote sensing. Radiation physics and spectral signatures. Radiation scattering. Image interpretation. Image processing. Ground truth data for quality assurance. Corequisite(s): CE 4331L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: GIS Applications in Engineering and Remote Sensing Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Data input and conversion. Spatial and network analysis. Digital image processing and interpretation. Project with civil engineering application.. Corequisite(s): CE 4331 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Foundation and Retaining Wall Design
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Analysis and design of spread footing foundations and cantilever retaining walls considering both geotechnical and structural aspects. Introduction to deep foundations.
courses.prerequisites: CE 326, CE 3401 , or ETC 411; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Pavement Design and Construction
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5451 Fundamental principles of structural pavement design and common design methods: AASHTO, Caltrans, Asphalt Institute and Portland Cement Association. Introduction to typical highway construction practices and activities. Laboratory testing of highway materials and quality assurance during construction are also discussed.
courses.prerequisites: CE 326, CE 3401 , or ETC 411; CE 221 or CE 2030 ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Slope Stability and Earth Dams
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CE 5470 General slope stability concepts. Soil strength and groundwater conditions. Slope stability analysis methods. Stability charts. Field investigation and instrumentation for landslide problems. Uncertainties in slope stability analysis and quantitative risk analysis. Slope stabilization methods. Earth dam analysis and design.
courses.prerequisites: ETC 411, CE 326, or CE 3401 ; ETC 411L, CE 327L, or CE 3401L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Structural Design - Reinforced Concrete
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: Analysis, design and detailing of reinforced concrete structural components including beams, slabs and columns; with emphasis on strength design theory and serviceability. Elements of integrated building design with primary emphasis on the impact of lateral forces on building stability.
courses.prerequisites: CE 2030 or CE 2030L ; ETC 311, CE 304, or CE 3501 ; CE 305L or CE 3501L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Structural Design - Steel
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6-7 units
courses.description: The theory and design of structural steel tension members, compression members, beams, beam-columns, simple connections, and eccentric connections. Design philosophies and probabilistic basis of load and resistance factors are discussed. This course prepares students for the effective use of the American Institute of Steel Construction Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD) specification.
courses.prerequisites: CE 2030 or CE 2030L ; ETC 311, CE 304, or CE 3501 ; CE 305L or CE 3501L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
